purpose: Developer-authored synthetic numerical diagnostics. No real sources, pilot annotations, independent labels or benchmark generalization are claimed.
policy: Compatible means interval overlap under the intended same measurement context, never entailment. Potential mismatch means disjoint values with intended matched context. Unresolved means insufficient/ambiguous context, units, scope or time. Hard paraphrase and multi-value cases have authored semantic expectations to expose conservative false abstentions.

cases.claim: Class A has 10 students.
cases.rationale: Same named population and count.

cases.claim: Class A pass rate in 2025 is 30%.

evidence.content: Class A pass rate in 2025 is 3%.

cases.rationale: Same property, population and year; non-overlapping exact percentages warrant review.

cases.claim: The bridge length is 1000 meters.
cases.rationale: Both normalize to 1000 meters.

cases.claim: Sensor A reading is 20 kilograms.
cases.rationale: Mass and distance are not commensurate measurements.

cases.claim: Class A pass rate in 2025 is about 30%.

evidence.content: Class A pass rate in 2025 is 29.8%.

cases.rationale: Within the documented diagnostic approximation band.

cases.claim: Class A pass rate in 2025 is roughly 30%.

evidence.content: Class A pass rate in 2025 is 3%.

cases.rationale: Far outside the declared approximation band in matched context.

cases.claim: Sensor A reading is 10 to 20 meters.

evidence.content: Sensor A reading is 15 to 25 meters.

cases.rationale: Range intersection is nonempty but does not establish the whole claim.

cases.claim: Sensor A reading is between 10 and 20 meters.

evidence.content: Sensor A reading is between 30 and 40 meters.

cases.rationale: Matched measurement context with disjoint intervals.

cases.claim: Class A score increased by 30%.

evidence.content: Class A score increased by 30 percentage points.

cases.rationale: Relative percentage and absolute percentage-point change require baseline information.

cases.claim: All students in Class A passed.

evidence.content: Some students in Class A passed.

cases.rationale: Some alone neither establishes nor refutes all.

cases.claim: No students in Class A passed.

evidence.content: Some students in Class A passed.

cases.rationale: Scope difference should be flagged without assuming population identity and forcing a verdict.

cases.claim: The lab opened in 2020.
cases.rationale: Calendar-year mismatch belongs to temporal analysis, not measurement arithmetic.

cases.claim: The array contains 2020 samples.
cases.rationale: Adjacent count noun distinguishes quantities from calendar years.

cases.claim: Sensor A temperature is 20°C.
cases.rationale: The same displayed number represents different temperatures after conversion.

cases.claim: Sensor A temperature is 20°C.
cases.rationale: Affine conversion yields the same temperature.

cases.claim: Class A has more than 10 students.
cases.rationale: The strict lower bound excludes exactly ten.

cases.claim: Class A has at least 10 students.
cases.rationale: An inclusive lower bound includes ten.

cases.claim: Class A has at most 10 students.
cases.rationale: Eleven exceeds the inclusive upper bound.

cases.claim: Sensor A temperature is -5.5°C.
cases.rationale: Signed decimal values match.

cases.claim: Class A has 10 students.

evidence.content: The Class A roster is unavailable.

cases.rationale: Missing quantities are not contradictions.

cases.claim: Class A has 10 students.
cases.rationale: Different named populations cannot be compared as one measurement.

cases.claim: Sample A mass is 10 kilograms.
cases.rationale: Matching units do not establish matching measured properties.

cases.claim: Class A has 10 students in 2020.
cases.rationale: Counts from different years need not conflict.

cases.claim: Class A students have a response rate of 30% in 2025.

evidence.content: Class A teachers have a response rate of 3% in 2025.

cases.rationale: The percentage applies to a different population.

cases.claim: Sample A length is 10m and Sample A mass is 2kg.

evidence.content: Sample A length is 0.01km and Sample A mass is 2000g.

cases.rationale: Separate properties retain equivalent normalized values in the surrounding frame.

cases.claim: Sample A length is 10m and Sample A mass is 2kg.

evidence.content: Sample A length is 12m and Sample A mass is 3kg.

cases.rationale: Authored same-property changes; retaining other values in context may make the implementation conservatively abstain.

cases.claim: Sample A mass is not 10 kilograms.
cases.rationale: Twenty is compatible with not-ten; the module must not force an opposite label from numeral differences.

cases.claim: Its mass is 10 kilograms.
cases.rationale: The pronoun does not establish shared entity identity.

cases.claim: The test bridge length is 1000 meters.

evidence.content: The measured span of the test bridge is 1 kilometer.

cases.rationale: Known constructed paraphrase; lexical context identity can miss this legitimate equivalence.

cases.claim: Class A has 10 students.
cases.rationale: The semantic count is equivalent, but digit-only extraction may miss the word ten.

cases.claim: Sample A mass is 1,5kg.
cases.rationale: A comma decimal is not silently repaired under an unspecified locale.

cases.claim: Class A currently has 10 students.
cases.rationale: Publication date alone does not anchor the source's current-status measurement.

cases.claim: Class A rate increased 30% from 100 samples.

evidence.content: Class A rate increased 30% from 200 samples.

cases.rationale: The same relative percentage with different baseline counts is unresolved; the explicit baseline counts themselves differ.

cases.claim: Not all students in Class A passed.

evidence.content: Some students in Class A passed.

cases.rationale: Some passing does not establish that not all passed; retain negation scope uncertainty.

cases.claim: The bridge length is from 1km to 1500m.
cases.rationale: Convert each compatible range endpoint before testing overlap.

cases.claim: Sensor A temperature is approximately 0°C.
cases.rationale: The declared absolute temperature floor handles zero without a meaningless relative tolerance.
